audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Lucian levels 2, 3, 6 and 2+ items while every why beside those rows says Camille takes over from level 2 onward.
audit.why: 25% win rate and the packet chart (Lucian/Camille x5/Skill) both say the same thing; the shipped rows were the outlier.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-6 flipped to Camille in matched full/content pairs, ratings pulled down, difficulty raised to 8/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 and 2+ items were written as Lucian spikes with boilerplate Culling copy.
audit.why: The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90s and anchors the target into a 1v1; Hookshot is 16s at rank 1 and needs terrain, which is the actual gate on her engage.
audit.corrected: Both rows now belong to Camille and name the real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly calls Tactical Sweep a true-damage cone; Adaptive Defenses and the Precision Protocol auto reset were absent.
audit.why: Riot's text puts the true damage on Precision Protocol (Q), which is also an auto reset and hits far harder if she delays between the two attacks. Tactical Sweep (W) damages, slows on the outer half and heals her from enemies hit there. Adaptive Defenses shields her against the damage type of whoever she attacks.
audit.corrected: True damage moved to Precision Protocol, Tactical Sweep described as the outer-half heal, shield-bait and the auto-reset tell added.

audit.why: The Hextech Ultimatum's derived untargetable and channel flags are not supported by Riot's description (dash, anchor, bonus magic damage on her attacks).
audit.corrected: No untargetability or interrupt claim written, despite the _missing rule suggesting one.

edits.before: Your one real window is Level 1: you have the auto range and the Lightslinger double-tap to win a short exchange before her E hookshot exists. Do it then back off. The moment she hits 2 the lane flips — her E stun catches your tiny base HP, her W cone is true damage that heals her through your Q poke, and her Q proc shreds. Never spend Relentless Pursuit chasing; that dash is your only answer to her E and you must keep it loaded. Last-hit at max Q range and do not walk into hookshot range to throw a Piercing Light you do not need.
edits.after: Your one real window is Level 1: you have the auto range and the Lightslinger double-tap to win a short exchange before Hookshot exists. Do it then back off. The moment she hits 2 the lane flips — Hookshot's knockup catches your tiny base HP, Tactical Sweep heals her off its outer half, and Precision Protocol's delayed second hit lands true damage straight through your armour. Never spend Relentless Pursuit chasing; that 16-second dash is your only answer to Hookshot, and Lightslinger hits are what shorten it. Last-hit at max Q range and stay off her walls.

edits.before: This is where you fall apart if you contest her. Once she has E up reliably she dictates every trade — she E-Qs onto you, true-damage cones you with W, and self-heals while your double-shot barely dents her. At 6 her R is the nightmare: it cages you into a 1v1 your dashes cannot escape, and inside that wall your kiting kit means nothing. Do not facecheck, do not greed a wave when she has R. Your job is to farm what you safely can and look to roam or set up a gank, because you do not win this duel anymore.
edits.after: This is where you fall apart if you contest her. Once Hookshot (16s at rank 1) is up reliably she dictates every trade — she hooks off a wall, Precision Protocol's delayed second hit lands true, and Tactical Sweep heals her while your double-shot barely dents her. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum is the nightmare: it anchors you into a 1v1 your dashes cannot escape. Do not facecheck walls, do not greed a wave when her R is up. Farm what you safely can and look to roam, because you do not win this duel anymore.

notes: Tactical Sweep was described as true damage in four places — the true damage belongs to Precision Protocol, which is also her auto reset. Both corrected. Packet suspectName "Hold Relentless Pursuit" is a FALSE POSITIVE: that is Lucian's real E. Row 6 set to Camille rather than the packet's "Skill" because the page's own whys[6] and late both describe her out-scaling outright; flag if the mirror disagrees. No untargetability claim written for her R — the derived flag contradicts Riot's text.
